items.title: Worthia "Showboy" Thomas Interview, 1961-12-11
items.q: Well he gave me my first lesson on the trombone. ... He taught me around Alexander for a little while.

ctx.x: How was he? How did they tell me he was a wonderful trombone? He was a great trombone player. Never made any records.

And he used to read pretty good. Great trombone player. Got a nice tone and he was real loud. He played loud. He played soft if it was necessary, but he naturally had a loud, he got a loud tone. Well he gave me my first lesson on the trombone. Well I started around Alexander on the trombone, playing a little. He taught me around Alexander for a little while. Then after, well I learned to play a few songs. After learning to play a few songs, I would take my trombone on the job with me when I go play drums. I had a…

We interviewed him a couple years ago. I forgot that he told us that he taught some pupils here. He probably mentioned you, no doubt. He did. I'd forgotten that. I was going to ask for how I think of it. Was there much difference in the music that you'd heard before you moved to New Orleans when you did come down here?
